Container.Name: Strata
Container.Overview:
Strata runs the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next mixture-of-experts model on one NVIDIA GPU plus system RAM, and serves an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, a chat page and a live monitor.
Requirements: the Nvidia Driver plugin on driver 580 or newer; an RTX 20/30/40/50 card with 12 GB of VRAM or more; an AVX2 CPU; 48-62 GB of free RAM depending on the model; 70-90 GB of disk on an SSD pool.
First start: downloads the model (about 70 GB for IQ2_XS) and sets it up, which can take a few hours. Watch the log; it resumes if it stops. Later starts go straight to serving, and loading the model into RAM takes 1-3 minutes.
Changing settings later: edit the template and apply. The new settings replace the saved ones on the next start; the model and the prepared pack stay in Data and are not downloaded again.
An API key is always on. Leave API key empty and the first start makes one and keeps it in Data; show it from the Unraid console with: docker exec Strata strata launch --show-key --preset docker
Upgrading from a 0.1.x image: the first start moves the existing model files into Data/Strata-data (a rename, nothing is downloaded again) and makes the run settings again from them.
This is an unofficial image built from Strata's own Dockerfile. Report template or image problems at the Support link, not to the Strata project.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: llm qwen local ai openai anthropic api inference chat nvidia cuda gpu
Container.Requires: **Nvidia Driver plugin** on driver 580 or newer. Do not pin CPUs: the engine sets its own thread affinity and breaks inside a cpuset. Do not set a memory limit: Strata plans from the server's total RAM, so a limit gets the container killed.

Config.Name: WebUI / API port
Config.Description: Chat page, monitor and the /v1 API. Requests need the API key; keep this LAN-only anyway.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The model, the prepared pack, the MTP layer, the saved settings and the API key: 70-90 GB depending on the model. Use a direct pool path (/mnt/cache/... or /mnt/POOLNAME/...), not /mnt/user: the engine reads experts from these files while it runs.

Config.Name: GPU
Config.Description: Your card's UUID (GPU-xxxxxxxx-...) from the Nvidia Driver plugin page or nvidia-smi -L. Name one card; 'all' on a two-card server makes setup split the model across both.

Config.Name: Model
Config.Description: IQ2_XS (recommended): 68 GB download, 48 GB RAM. Q2_0: fastest, 48 GB RAM (qwen only). IQ3_XXS: better, 60 GB RAM. IQ3_S: best quality, 62 GB RAM. IQ1_M: coder family only, 32 GB RAM. UD-Q4_K_XL: unsloth family only.

Config.Name: Model family
Config.Description: qwen (default); swift (thinks shorter); coder (for code, fewer experts); unsloth and nvfp4 need their own models (see Model).

Config.Name: Context length
Config.Description: Tokens per conversation. Longer costs RAM; setup caps it if the RAM is short.

Config.Name: Vision
Config.Description: Image input: gpu runs the image encoder on the GPU, cpu runs it on the CPU. The encoder (about 0.9 GB) is downloaded with the model.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: 16 characters or more (openssl rand -hex 24 makes one). Empty = the first start makes one and keeps it in Data; the log says how to show it. Clients send it as Authorization: Bearer; /health answers without it.

Config.Name: KV cache type
Config.Description: int8 (default); q4_0 halves the KV memory, slightly less precise; k8v4 keeps its KV in VRAM from 64K context up; fp16 is full precision and needs the most memory.

Config.Name: NVIDIA driver capabilities
Config.Description: Must include utility: setup needs nvidia-smi.
